> # SwiftShader Command-Line Switches for Chromium
> 
> ## OpenGL ES Driver (SwANGLE)
> **Switch:** `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader`
> 
> **Purpose:** "When Chromium uses SwiftShader as the OpenGL ES driver, Chromium behaves as if it was running a on regular GPU, while actually running on SwiftShader."
> 
> ## WebGL Fallback (SwANGLE - Unsafe)
> **Switch:** `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader-webgl --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`
> 
> **Purpose:** "When Chromium uses SwiftShader as the WebGL fallback, Chromium runs in all software mode and only uses SwiftShader to render WebGL content."
> 
> **Deprecation Note:** "Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader has been deprecated and WebGL context creation will soon fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader." The `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader` flag allows users to opt-in despite security concerns.
> 
> ## Vulkan Driver
> **Switch:** `--use-vulkan=swiftshader`
> 
> **Requirement:** Requires the enable_swiftshader_vulkan feature to be enabled.
> 
> **Key Security Warning:** "SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process."
> ```

> ## Headless Rendering with Three.js
> 
> **Headless-gl Approach**: Developers have used headless-gl with Jest unit testing to render frames using WebGLRenderer.render() just like a browser environment. However, since THREE deprecated WebGL1 in version 0.163.0, headless-gl can't be used anymore since the package doesn't support WebGL2.
> 
> **Off-screen Rendering Techniques**: One approach uses WebGLRenderTarget to store off-screen rendered pixel data in a buffer area. You can render data cached in WebGLRenderTarget onto a canvas and output base64 image data using Canvas toDataURL() or canvas.toBlob().
> 
> **Software Rendering Alternative**: For GPU-independent rendering, there's a SoftwareRenderer that's a drop-in renderer for Three.js that can be used on the server and client, though it's much slower than the WebGLRenderer since it doesn't have access to GPU acceleration.
> 
> **Server-side Rendering**: For serverless 3D rendering in AWS Lambda, a custom-built Chromium version is needed to handle the headless browser.

> ## Overview

> The `--deterministic-mode` flag is an experimental meta flag that puts the browser into a mode where rendering (border radius, etc) is deterministic and begin frames should be issued over DevTools Protocol.
> 
> ## The Flags Explained
> 
> The `--deterministic-mode` flag sets several sub-flags including `--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw`, `--disable-new-content-rendering-timeout`, `--enable-begin-frame-control`, `--disable-threaded-animation`, `--disable-threaded-scrolling`, and `--disable-checker-imaging`.
> 
> **Individual flag purposes:**
> 
> - **`--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw`**: This flag ensures that the compositor does not prematurely commit display frames that are missing some compositing updates.
> 
> - **`--disable-new-content-rendering-timeout`**: Part of the deterministic mode set that helps control rendering timing.
> 
> ## Use Case with Screenshots
> 
> This approach is designed for use with `--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw`. When these flags are used together, every one turns off a source of async scheduling, and the compositor runs synchronously on the main thread and does not advance until Chrome DevTools Protocol tells it to.
> 
> These flags are particularly useful for reliably capturing screenshots in headless Chrome automation scenarios where you need consistent, predictable rendering.
> 
> 
> REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.
> ```

> # transform-style: preserve-3d
> 
> ## What It Does
> 
> According to the MDN documentation:
> 
> > "Indicates that the children of the element should be positioned in the 3D-space."
> 
> ## Properties That Force Flattening
> 
> Even when `preserve-3d` is specified, certain property values force the element to have a used value of `transform-style: flat`. The spec lists these "grouping property values":
> 
> - **`overflow`**: any value other than `visible` or `clip`
> - **`opacity`**: any value less than `1`
> - **`filter`**: any value other than `none`
> - **`clip`**: any value other than `auto`
> - **`clip-path`**: any value other than `none`
> - **`isolation`**: used value of `isolate`
> - **`mask-image`**: any value other than `none`
> - **`mask-border-source`**: any value other than `none`
> - **`mix-blend-mode`**: any value other than `normal`
> - **`contain`**: `paint` and any other property/value combination that causes paint containment (including `content-visibility: hidden`)
> 
> These properties require the user agent to create a flattened representation of the descendant elements before they can be applied, which overrides the `preserve-3d` setting.
> ```
